title: Shadows, Reflection and Refraction
seo_title: Year 5 Science: Shadows, Reflection and Refraction Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe how light travels from a source and how it interacts with objects and materials to form shadows and images, including reflection and refraction (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 5 science worksheets on shadows, reflection and refraction: shadows in the Australian sun, mirrors and periscopes, bent straws, magnifying glasses and rainbows. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Light is blocked, bounced or bent.
key_sub: Shadows form when light is blocked; reflection bounces light; refraction bends it.
body_html:
How to think about it

When light meets an object, it can be blocked, reflected or refracted.

  • A shadow forms where an opaque object blocks light. In southern Australia, the midday Sun is in the north, so shadows are short and point south.
  • Reflection: light bounces off a surface. Smooth, shiny surfaces such as mirrors reflect light well.
  • Refraction: light bends when it passes from air into water or glass. A straw looks bent; a pool looks shallower.
Example

A flagpole at 9 am. Which way does its shadow point?

the Sun is in the east

the shadow points away from the Sun

Answer: towards the west

Example

A straw looks bent in water. Why?

light passes from water into air

it bends at the surface

Answer: refraction

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a shadow is a reflection of the object (it is where light is missing).
  • Thinking shadows are longest at midday (they are shortest).
  • Mixing up reflection (bouncing) and refraction (bending).

faq.q: Why do shadows in Sydney point south at midday?
faq.a: Sydney is in the southern hemisphere, south of the tropics, so the midday Sun is always in the northern part of the sky. Shadows point away from the Sun, towards the south.

faq.q: What is the difference between reflection and refraction?
faq.a: Reflection is light bouncing off a surface, such as a mirror. Refraction is light bending as it passes from one material into another, such as from water into air.
Sunlight shines into raindrops. The light is refracted (bent) and split into colours: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

items.q: A torch shines on a hand with fingers spread. What shape is its shadow?
c: a hand shape with spread fingers
items.e: Light travels in straight lines, so the shadow has the same outline as the object.

items.q: Oliver is making shadows on a screen with a vase. Oliver moves the torch further from the vase. What happens to the shadow?
c: The shadow stays the same size.
items.e: The closer the object is to the light, the more light it blocks, so the shadow is bigger.

items.q: How is a shadow made?
c: An opaque object blocks light, leaving a dark area behind it.
The object reflects its colour onto the ground.
items.e: Light travels in straight lines, so it cannot reach behind the object.

How many mirrors does a simple periscope use?
items.e: One at the top and one at the bottom.

items.q: What happens when light hits a mirror?
c: It reflects (bounces off) in a new direction.
items.e: Smooth, shiny surfaces reflect light well.

items.q: What does a periscope let you do?
items.e: Light is reflected twice.

items.q: At what angle are the mirrors in a periscope set?
items.e: Each mirror turns the light through a right angle.

items.q: A ray of light hits a flat mirror at 45° to the normal (the line at right angles to the mirror). At what angle does it reflect?
items.e: The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.

items.q: Which of these reflects the most light: a dark wooden log, a grey felt hat, a navy blue towel or a new coin?
items.e: Smooth, shiny and light-coloured surfaces reflect the most light.

items.q: Why do lifesavers wear bright, reflective vests?
c: They absorb heat from the sun.
They reflect lots of light, so people can see them easily.
items.e: Bright colours reflect more light.

items.q: Which surface reflects the least light?
items.e: Dark, rough surfaces absorb most light.

items.q: Which of these reflects the least light: a new coin, a piece of dark brown cardboard, a polished silver tray or a sheet of kitchen foil?
c: a piece of dark brown cardboard
items.e: Dark, dull and rough surfaces reflect very little light.

items.q: You hold a book up to a mirror. What happens to the writing?
c: It appears back to front (reversed left to right).
items.e: Mirror images are reversed.

items.q: A ray of light hits a flat mirror at 40° to the normal (the line at right angles to the mirror). At what angle does it reflect?
items.e: The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.

items.q: Which of these reflects the most light: a grey felt hat, a muddy football, a navy blue towel or a polished silver tray?
items.e: Smooth, shiny and light-coloured surfaces reflect the most light.

items.q: Why is AMBULANCE written backwards on the front of ambulances?
c: so drivers can read it the right way in their mirrors
so only nurses can read it
items.e: Mirrors reverse left and right.

items.q: Which of these reflects the least light: a mirror, a new coin, a piece of black paper or a still pond?
items.e: Dark, dull and rough surfaces reflect very little light.

items.q: Which of these reflects the most light: a black woolly jumper, a lump of black coal, a piece of black paper or a shiny metal spoon?
items.e: Smooth, shiny and light-coloured surfaces reflect the most light.

items.q: Why do we see our reflection in a mirror but not in a brick wall?
c: A mirror is smooth and shiny, so the reflected light stays in order.
items.e: Rough surfaces scatter light in all directions.

items.q: A ray of light hits a flat mirror at 10° to the normal (the line at right angles to the mirror). At what angle does it reflect?
items.e: The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.

items.q: Which of these reflects the most light: a black sock, a muddy football, a navy blue towel or a polished silver tray?
items.e: Smooth, shiny and light-coloured surfaces reflect the most light.

items.q: Which of these reflects the most light: a black woolly jumper, a glossy white tile, a navy blue towel or a piece of black paper?
items.e: Smooth, shiny and light-coloured surfaces reflect the most light.

items.q: Which surface reflects light best to give a clear image?
items.e: Smooth surfaces reflect light evenly.

items.q: A tree blocks sunlight and leaves a dark patch on the ground. Which word best explains this?
items.e: A shadow forms where an opaque object blocks light.

items.q: Which is an example of refraction, not reflection?
c: a spoon looking bent in a glass of water
a shiny spoon showing your face
seeing yourself in a window at night
items.e: Bending is refraction; bouncing is reflection.

items.q: Which part of the eye refracts light to make a clear image?
items.e: The lens bends light onto the back of the eye.

items.q: A coin at the bottom of a cup cannot be seen. Water is poured in and the coin appears. Why?
c: Light from the coin bends at the water surface towards your eye.
items.e: This is a classic refraction test.

items.q: What tool splits sunlight into a spectrum of colours?
items.e: Prisms refract light.

items.q: Your hand blocks a torch and a dark shape appears on the wall. Which word best explains this?
items.e: A shadow forms where an opaque object blocks light.

items.q: Your legs look shorter when you stand in a clear pool. Which word best explains this?
items.e: Refraction: light bends as it passes from one material (such as water or glass) into another.

items.q: How does a magnifying glass work?
c: It reflects light like a mirror.
Its curved glass bends (refracts) light so things look bigger.
items.e: A lens refracts light.

items.q: Where must the Sun be for you to see a rainbow?
c: behind you, with rain in front of you
items.e: Sunlight goes past you into the raindrops.

items.q: You see your face in a still lake. Which word best explains this?
items.e: Reflection: light bounces off a surface.

items.q: Which of these causes a rainbow?
items.e: Refraction splits white light into colours.

items.q: Why does a pool look shallower than it is?
c: Light from the bottom bends as it leaves the water.
The water is thicker at the bottom.
Light reflects off the bottom twice.
items.e: Take care: the water is deeper than it looks.

items.q: White light passes through raindrops and makes a rainbow. Which word best explains this?
items.e: Refraction: light bends as it passes from one material (such as water or glass) into another.

items.q: A straw in a glass of water looks bent where it enters the water. Which word best explains this?
items.e: Refraction: light bends as it passes from one material (such as water or glass) into another.

items.q: Light goes from air into water. What happens?
c: It goes round in a circle.
items.e: Light travels more slowly in water.

items.q: Glasses (spectacles) help people see clearly. Which word best explains this?
items.e: Refraction: light bends as it passes from one material (such as water or glass) into another.

items.q: Why do people who spearfish aim below where the fish seems to be?
c: Refraction makes the fish look higher than it really is.
items.e: Light bends at the water's surface.

items.q: Which colours make up white light?
c: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet
items.e: A prism splits white light into these colours.

items.q: What does a glass prism do to a beam of white light?
c: It bends it and splits it into colours.
items.e: This is refraction.

items.q: The Moon shines in the night sky. Which word best explains this?
items.e: Reflection: light bounces off a surface.

items.q: How could a shadow puppet show make one puppet look like a giant?
c: move that puppet closer to the light
move it next to the screen
items.e: Use the pattern.

items.q: Which of these reflects the least light: a bicycle reflector, a dark carpet, a mirror or a shiny metal spoon?
items.e: Dark, dull and rough surfaces reflect very little light.

items.q: A student says shadows are reflections. How could you show they are not?
c: A shadow has no colour or detail, but a reflection shows the object's colours.
items.e: Compare them.

items.q: A torch is in front of a wooden block. Where is its shadow?
c: on the left of the object
on the right of the object
items.e: A shadow forms on the opposite side of the object from the light.

items.q: A swimming pool looks shallower than it really is. Which word best explains this?
items.e: Refraction: light bends as it passes from one material (such as water or glass) into another.

items.q: A magnifying glass makes an ant look bigger. Which word best explains this?
items.e: Refraction: light bends as it passes from one material (such as water or glass) into another.

items.q: Road signs glow brightly at night in headlights. Which word best explains this?
items.e: Reflection: light bounces off a surface.

items.q: Why do sundials work?
c: The Sun's shadow moves in a regular way during the day.
items.e: The Earth turns.

items.q: Kai wants to find which surface reflects the most light. Which is the fairest test?
c: a different torch for each surface
testing in daylight and at night
the same torch at the same distance and angle on each surface, with a light meter
items.e: Keep everything the same except the surface.

items.q: A bike reflector shines when car headlights hit it. Which word best explains this?
items.e: Reflection: light bounces off a surface.

items.q: Which of these reflects the least light: a muddy football, a sheet of kitchen foil, a shiny metal spoon or a still pond?
items.e: Dark, dull and rough surfaces reflect very little light.

items.q: Ruby puts a coin in a bowl and steps back until she cannot see it. Ella pours in water slowly. What will Ruby see?
items.e: Refraction bends light from the coin into her eyes.

items.q: Mia measures a 1 m stick's shadow every hour. At 9 am it is 2.5 m, at 12 noon 0.4 m and at 3 pm 2.2 m. What pattern does she see?
c: The shadow is shortest around midday.
The shadow gets longer all day.
The shadow is longest at midday.
items.e: The Sun is highest at midday.

items.q: In Jack's test, what should he keep the same?
c: the torch, the toy and the screen position
items.e: Only the distance should change.

items.q: A torch is in front of a model house. Where is its shadow?
c: on the left of the object
on the right of the object
items.e: A shadow forms on the opposite side of the object from the light.

items.q: Why do some cars have a rear-view mirror that is curved outwards?
c: It refracts light like a lens.
It reflects light from a wider area, so the driver sees more.
items.e: Curved mirrors spread out the view.

items.q: Dark clothes feel warmer on a sunny day. Which word best explains this?
items.e: Absorption: the material takes in the light, and it warms up.

items.q: Why are there two shadows when two lamps shine on one object?
c: Each lamp's light is blocked separately, making one shadow each.
items.e: One shadow per light source.

items.q: A torch is on the left of a jug. Where is its shadow?
c: on the left of the object
on the right of the object
items.e: A shadow forms on the opposite side of the object from the light.

items.q: Why do drivers have mirrors on cars?
c: to see behind them by reflecting light into their eyes
items.e: Reflection in use.
